reason: Each rule compares a directory's file or subdirectory count to a threshold (2.25x the sibling median, 60%+ tiny files, more than twenty files or ten child dirs) and selects the directory; none says which files fail to share a concern.

Each rule combines a complexity measure with churn or growth into a score (hotspot quadrant, churn x complexity with ownership signals, or >20% file growth) to rank code; the score selects attention and never names an unnecessary structure.

Each rule states the failure directly: new code reinvents infrastructure the codebase already provides, a GenServer reimplements a key-value store that Agent or ETS already offers, or custom code reimplements established library functionality.
The single rule names the failure: a React useEffect whose body only calls setState, copying source state into a second state through an effect instead of deriving it during render.

The single rule matches fallback/workaround phrases in the agent's text with a PreToolUse regex before any code exists; it matches wording and never inspects a delivered structure, so it only selects text for review.

Most rules name a structure whose variation is never exercised: a single-implementation interface, a constant-output factory, a single-use file, a stateless class, an over-complex generic bound, and speculative abstraction. The entry's kind is candidate pattern; rule 092 is conditional on a finished migration and rule 113 only counts public methods.

misfit_rules.reason: It flags deprecated-but-called symbols and mixed old/new APIs without checking whether the migration is finished, so it is slop only under the added condition that no caller still needs the old API.
It counts public methods (exactly one besides __init__) and calls it a premature-abstraction signal, without showing the class provides no boundary.

reason: Each rule names a placement or dependency that breaks a declared or inferred architectural rule: a backward/cross-boundary import, a wrong-layer import, a contract defined beside its implementation, an upward or denied dependency edge, a function whose purpose does not match its file, and a file in a forbidden directory.

Most rules name a split between a responsibility and its owning unit: feature envy, inappropriate intimacy, a data class with no behavior, divergent change, shotgun surgery, and feature logic scattered across layers. Rule 555 instead matches generic module names, so the entry's kind is candidate pattern.

misfit_rules.reason: It matches the module names utils/helpers/common/shared rather than verifying the module actually collects unrelated functions.

reason: The single rule names the failure: a subclass override that signals not-implemented or unsupported, or that strengthens preconditions or weakens postconditions, so it breaks the parent contract.

Every rule selects a function, class, or file by comparing a size or complexity count (lines, parameters, nesting, cyclomatic/cognitive/NPath/Halstead/WMC complexity, divider comments, Gini concentration, CRAP, export count) to a threshold; none says which structure is unnecessary.

Each rule names a boundary directive that does not match the code: 'use client' on a file using no client APIs, a directive placed where it has no effect, and a barrel that mixes client and server modules under one import.
Both rules name a concrete route-identity conflict: two route files resolving to one URL, and sibling dynamic segments at one tree position using different parameter names.

The single rule names the failure: test classes that mirror production's per-method structure and assert one behavior through several internal paths, coupling the suite to internals so a behavior-preserving refactor breaks it.

The single rule measures service-to-service call-chain depth and fires when it exceeds three hops; the depth count is read as a sign of a missing aggregation layer rather than naming the hop that should not exist.

Most rules name a library unit reaching past its scope and check the library context: a service-locator get/set over global state, sys.exit outside CLI entry points, os.Exit/Setenv/panic in pkg/*, and the stdlib logger in pkg/*. The entry's kind is candidate pattern; rules 154 and 158 flag mechanisms that are legitimate in an entry point without checking that it is a library.

misfit_rules.reason: It matches the global keyword and package-level mutable vars everywhere, which is slop only under the added condition that the code is a reusable library unit rather than a process entry point.
It flags import-time side effects in any module, which is slop only under the added condition that the module is a library unit, not an entry point or a plugin that requires import-time registration.

condition: the mismatch with the repository's existing patterns is structural, such as a hand-written client beside generated ones, rather than naming, logging, error-handling, or test style
reason: The single rule checks a change against the repository's existing patterns, naming, error handling, logging, and test style in one pass and does not separate which part it found, so it is a structural failure only when the mismatch it flags is itself structural.

Every rule measures the shape of a dependency, inheritance, or render graph (coupling between objects, inheritance depth and width, package distance, modularity, dependency depth, unstable coupling, propagation cost, render fan-in) against a threshold; the measurement selects an architecture for review instead of naming the edge that should not be there.
Both rules name a declared dependency with no provider on any reaching path: a parameter or option field that no caller ever passes, and an inject/getContext key that no ancestor provides.

Both rules name computation tangled with effects: input interpretation mixed with execution inside a loop, and business calculation mixed with database, HTTP, logging, or file I/O instead of being isolated in pure functions.

The single rule names a data clump: the same parameter group recurring across three or more signatures, a concept traveling as loose values that should be one type. The count of three is a threshold, while the stated failure is the repeated group itself.

Both rules name the failure, a call chain that walks several links through objects the caller never received (a.b().c().d()); one adds a classification pipeline that excludes fluent, module-qualified, and traversal chains, and the weaker detector still states the same navigation failure.

Each rule names an expression step that cannot change the result: an identity match or map, an if that rebuilds the boolean it tested, a variable read once on the next line, a two-call pipeline one library call replaces, a redundant await, and an IIFE wrapping code that could run directly.

Two rules name a circular module dependency directly, through value imports and through re-export chains. The entry's kind is candidate pattern; rule 089 flags function-level imports whether or not a cycle exists.

misfit_rules.reason: It flags function-level (deferred) imports generally, which is a cycle failure only under the added condition that the deferred import exists to hide a cycle rather than to lazily load an optional, heavy, or platform-specific module.

reason: Most rules name a published surface the boundary does not own: a wildcard re-export that republishes whatever its target holds, a service returning its persistence entity, and an exported signature naming a private type. The entry's kind is candidate pattern; rule 079 identifies a re-export-only file without checking it is a published boundary.

misfit_rules.reason: It identifies a file consisting only of re-exports, which is a non-owned surface only under the added condition that the file is a published package boundary rather than an internal barrel or a facade released as a union of its submodules.

reason: The single rule names the failure: a shared abstraction that has accumulated a branch for each caller's special case, so the branching now costs more than the duplication it removed.
The single rule counts a suite's tests against a budget of twice the number of distinct behaviors and fires when the count is exceeded; the count does not show which tests are redundant.

Each rule names an effect hidden from the call site: a getter with side effects, in-place mutation of a parameter, a command disguised as a query, a service locator, validation that throws as control flow, and side effects delegated to an opaque function.

Each rule names an interposed unit that forwards its payload unchanged: a thin pass-through wrapper, an async function with nothing to await, a rename-only adapter, a delegating middle man, a generic status envelope, props drilled through non-consuming components, and identical-shape DTO round-trips.

Each rule names variant selection done by branches inside a shared body: repeated equality or isinstance ladders, if/elif chains without exhaustiveness, a boolean flag choosing between two behaviors, and type-tag branches every new variant must extend.
